subject: Various obsCovs errors in creating unmarkedFrameGMM

messages.author: 1b830cb6535ef59f
messages.subject: Various obsCovs errors in creating unmarkedFrameGMM
parts:
I have what I think is a fairly straightforward problem with formatting my obsCovs correctly for creation of an unmarkedFrameGMM.

I'm using point counts of birds at ~840 sites with 1-3 visits at each site and 3 subintervals for each visit. The data is formatted for each species with rows of each site and columns of each visit and subinterval (i.e., 1-1, 1-2, 1-3, 2-1, etc.). The siteCovs is similar with rows of each site and columns of different variables (canopy, chaparral, etc.). Those two pieces seem to fit fine with the data loaded as a matrix and the siteCovs loaded as a data frame. 

Now the obsCovs--I initially created a table with with rows of site-visit-subinterval and columns of the variables (noise, surveyor, Julian date, and minutes past sunrise) because that's what it seemed the help file was telling me. I simply assigned that table to the object obsCovs and when building my unmarkedFrameGMM used obsCovs=obsCovs. That returned the error that 
"invalid class "unmarkedFrame" object: obsCovData does not have M*obsNum rows." 
I then tried entering it as the help file later suggests by setting occasion equal to my data: 
obsCovs=list(occasion=obsCovs)
which gave the error:
"At least one matrix in obsCovs has incorrect number of dimensions"
Finally I tried importing a csv for each observation covariate separately and in the same form as the data and the siteCovs (with rows of site and columns of visit-subinterval). I made a list of those (as suggested by a previous post in this group) and input them in the same two ways I tried previously with the same error messages. I've tried several permutations of these methods and I keep getting the same two error messages.

So I guess my big question is can someone clarify in what form my obsCovs need to be in order for R to be satisfied? The help file is extremely unclear and I am completely new to R.

Thanks!

 the help file for unmarkedFrameGMM has an example of such a covariate and the dimension of the input covariate in that case is nsites x (J*T)  -- in that case 50 x 12
 But I don't think that's how you organized your covariates.... try doing that and see if it works.
regards
andy

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Various obsCovs errors in creating unmarkedFrameGMM
parts:
Hi Caitlin, if you look at obsCovs(umfGMM1) in the example for unmarkedMultFrame, you'll see that the single covariate "occasion" is ultimately formatted as an MTJ vector by the umf function.  But when you create the umf you can either specify the obsCovs covariates in long format (single MTJ vector) as a data frame, or wide format (M by TJ matrix) as a list.  You cannot specify the long format as a list.  I think most folks work with the wide format since it is easier to envision, but unmarked uses the long format during model fitting for increased speed.  Here are the options:

# wide format

...obsCovs=list(occasion=occasions)

# long format
occasions <- as.vector(t(data.frame(matrix(rep(1:(J*T), each=n), n, J*T))))
...obsCovs=data.frame(occasion=occasions)

Understanding the structure of a list, data frame, array, matrix, etc. is a tricky but important part of R (and programming in general).  There are many webpages with helpful explanations.
